sentences.ar: النهاردة إحنا هنغوص في عالم الداتا وتحديدا هنفكك معمارية منصة هواوي DataCube
sentences.en: Today we dive into the world of data and specifically take apart the architecture of the Huawei DataCube platform.

sentences.ar: هنشوف مع بعض إزاي المنصة دي بتاخد raw operational data يعني بيانات التشغيل الخام والملغبطة جدا وتعملها سحر كده
sentences.en: We'll see how this platform takes raw operational data, the raw and very messy operating data, and works magic on it.

sentences.ar: عشان تحولها لbusiness intelligence ورؤية واضحة جدا وتحديدا لخدمات الـMobile Money
sentences.en: So it turns it into business intelligence and a very clear view, specifically for mobile money services.

sentences.ar: الموضوع فعلا أشبه بهندسة عبقرية
sentences.en: The subject really is like brilliant engineering.

sentences.ar: هنمشي مع البيانات من أول ما تدخل السيستم لحد ما تخرج في شكل تأرير
sentences.en: We'll walk with the data from the moment it enters the system until it comes out as a report.

sentences.ar: وهنعدي على خمس محطات الـArchitecture الـstar schema المطبخ بتاعنا ال -ETL وبعدين ال -Daily Report وهنخدم بال -Governance وال -Masking
sentences.en: We'll pass through five stations: architecture, the star schema, our kitchen the ETL, then the Daily Report, and we'll serve it with Governance and Masking.

sentences.ar: خلينا ندخل في الموضوع على طول ونبدأ بأول محطة الـArchitecture وال -Storage
sentences.en: Let's get straight into it and start with the first station, architecture and storage.

sentences.ar: إزاي بنبني الأساس اللي هيشيل كل ده؟
sentences.en: How do we build the foundation that will carry all of this?

sentences.ar: تخيالوا معايا كده إزاي ممكن ناخد أكتر من 50 مصدر بيانات خام ونحولهم لرؤية بيزنس واضح
sentences.en: Imagine with me how we could take more than 50 raw data sources and turn them into a clear business view.

sentences.ar: التحدي هنا مش بس في العدد لا التحدي في السرعات
sentences.en: The challenge here is not only the count; the challenge is the speeds.

sentences.ar: يعني احنا بنسحب بيانات من منصة الـMobile Money كل 15 دقيقة ومن الـbilling كل ساعة ومن الـCRM مرة كل يوم
sentences.en: We pull data from the Mobile Money platform every 15 minutes, from billing every hour, and from CRM once a day.

sentences.ar: فوضى صح؟ كل مصدر ليه إيقاعه الخاص وده بيمثل تحدي ضخم جدا
sentences.en: Chaos, right? Every source has its own rhythm, and that represents a huge challenge.

sentences.ar: الحل بيبدأ من هنا
sentences.en: The solution starts from here.

sentences.ar: الـDataCube مش مجرد dashboard منفصلة بنبص عليه وخلاص دي معمارية كاملة بتشتغل كـpipeline متصل
sentences.en: DataCube is not just a separate dashboard we look at and that's it; it's a complete architecture running as a connected pipeline.

sentences.ar: بتبدأ من الـSources بعدها بتعدي على طبقة ال -ETL للدمج والتنظيف
sentences.en: It starts from the sources, then passes through the ETL layer for merging and cleaning.

sentences.ar: بعدين بتدخل في ال -Storage Layers عشان تتخزن وفي النهاية بتوصل لطبقة ال -Analytics وال -Reporting
sentences.en: Then it enters the storage layers to be stored, and finally reaches the analytics and reporting layer.

sentences.ar: خطوة بخطوة الفوضى دي بتتحول للنظام دقيق
sentences.en: Step by step, this chaos turns into a precise system.

sentences.ar: الجدول ده بيوضح تأسيمه بزكاء جدا عندنا ثلاث طبقات للتخزين
sentences.en: The table shows its division very cleverly: we have three storage layers.

sentences.en: First the ODS, which is for raw data with retention of just days, and it is used by the ETL developers.

sentences.ar: ثانياً ال -DW أو Data Warehouse وده بقى بيحتفظ بتاريخ كامل لسنين وبيستخدمه الـanalysts
sentences.en: Second the DW, or Data Warehouse, which keeps a full history for years and is used by the analysts.

sentences.ar: وأخيراً الـData Mart وده بيقدم ملخصات جاهزة لأقسام معينة وتاريخه بالشهور وموجه أكتر لمديرين البزنس

sentences.ar: كل واحد وليه استخدام
sentences.en: Each one has its own use.

sentences.ar: وما فيش storage واحد ينفع لكل حاجة صح؟
sentences.en: And no single storage fits everything, right?

sentences.ar: شجرة القرار دي بتوضح نستخدم إيه وإمتى

glossary.rule: Explain the term in Egyptian Arabic the first time it appears; then use the original term naturally, in Latin script, inside Arabic sentences.
glossary.register_ar: Natural Egyptian, clear, calm, professional. Use إحنا and خلّينا نشوف and ببساطة where they help. No heavy Modern Standard Arabic. No exaggerated slang. Numbers are spoken naturally in Egyptian but displayed as Western digits.
glossary.register_en: Plain, direct, unhurried. Short sentences. No hype, no "imagine that…", no rhetorical questions that are not real prediction prompts. Say the number, then pause for half a beat before the next sentence — the pause is where the viewer reads the screen.
glossary.never_translate_rule: Explain them in Egyptian Arabic the first time they appear, then use the original term naturally.
glossary.on_screen: Western digits, Latin terms in LTR isolates, Egyptian Arabic copy (no MSA), no per-letter animation (04 section 3.4).

concepts.def_en: Huawei's analytics and reporting platform for large data: a connected pipeline from sources through warehouse layers to BI reports, not just a dashbo…
concepts.failure: Mistaking DataCube for just a dashboard, ignoring the pipeline and layers behind it.

concepts.def_en: Financial services over a mobile phone, such as wallets, transfers and cash in/out, run by providers like the fictional NilePay in this course.
concepts.failure: Treating balances as a simple column update; money movement needs atomic, auditable transactions.

concepts.def_en: A warehouse design with one central fact table of measures joined directly to surrounding dimension tables, forming a star shape.
concepts.failure: Joining two fact tables directly, which multiplies rows and inflates totals.

concepts.def_en: Extract, Transform, Load: pull data from sources, clean and reshape it first, then load the finished result into the target.
concepts.failure: Discarding the raw data after transforming, so mistakes cannot be replayed.

concepts.def_en: The declared structure of data: field or column names, types and constraints, which a table or message must follow.
concepts.failure: Changing a field's type or removing it without checking that downstream consumers still work.

concepts.def_en: The durable layer where data persists after programs stop, such as disks or a warehouse, separate from ingestion and presentation.
concepts.failure: Treating ingestion, storage and presentation as one step, so ownership and debugging get blurred.

concepts.def_en: A single screen of charts and key numbers that lets people monitor metrics and make decisions quickly from data.
concepts.failure: Cramming many unrelated charts together, so viewers cannot see what to act on.

concepts.def_en: A chain of automated steps where each stage's output feeds the next, such as extract, transform and load for data.
concepts.failure: Not making steps idempotent, so a rerun duplicates or corrupts data.

concepts.def_en: Operational Data Store: a layer close to the source that keeps its shape, holding raw data for a short retention, used by ETL developers.
concepts.failure: Using the ODS for long-term analytics instead of a short-retention raw layer.

concepts.def_en: A central store of cleaned, integrated, historical data from many sources, organized for analysis rather than daily transactions.
concepts.failure: Treating it as a plain copy of the operational database, without modelling for analysis.

concepts.def_en: A subject-focused slice of the warehouse for one department or domain, offering ready summaries close to the people who ask.
concepts.failure: Building separate marts with conflicting metric definitions, so departments report different revenue.

concepts.def_en: A group of records processed together in one run, as opposed to streaming; a batch identifier makes reloads safe to repeat.
concepts.failure: Rerunning a batch load without deleting that batch first, duplicating rows.

concepts.def_en: Huawei's distributed relational database, built on MPP shared-nothing architecture, used here for analytical queries over large historical data and f…
concepts.failure: Using it like a single-node database and ignoring distribution key choice.

concepts.def_en: Hadoop Distributed File System: splits files into blocks spread across DataNodes and keeps several replicas of each on different machines.
concepts.failure: Storing huge numbers of tiny files, which overload the NameNode's metadata memory.

concepts.def_en: What exactly one row represents, such as one order line; every metric must be computed at that level.
concepts.failure: Computing a SUM at the wrong grain, getting a confident but wrong number.

concepts.def_en: Adding reference data or business rules to an event or record, such as customer, service and region details, to make it ready for reporting.
concepts.failure: Joining today's reference values to old events, which rewrites history.

concepts.def_en: After loading, comparing source and target counts and totals to prove nothing was lost, duplicated or changed; any mismatch is investigated.
concepts.failure: Assuming a green job run means every row arrived, without comparing counts and totals.

concepts.def_en: Mobile Station International Subscriber Directory Number: the full mobile phone number that identifies a subscriber, treated as PII and masked in rep…
concepts.failure: Storing or showing the full number in reports instead of masking it.

concepts.def_en: Personally identifiable information: data that can identify a specific person, such as name, phone number or national ID.
concepts.failure: Assuming masking one field is enough, when combined fields can still re-identify a person.

concepts.def_en: Transport Layer Security: a handshake that proves the server's identity and encrypts data in transit between client and server.
concepts.failure: Skipping certificate verification, which leaves traffic encrypted but possibly sent to an impostor.

components.does: One whole word (or a tatweel-joined compound like الـKafka) on screen; never split per letter.
Up to 6 kinetic words on at most 2 lines, each word arriving on its own spoken word anchor.
A technical term chip (Latin in an LTR isolate) with an optional Arabic gloss; 28 px floor if spoken.
A counter that rolls from the previous value to the target over the spoken number (preset count).
An arrow from a label to a target layer (or a named part of it, 'layer.part').
Failure beat: glitch + low thud; flashes stay <= 3/s (WCAG 2.3.1).
Fix beat: the target settles into place with a settle chime.
The shot camera: move + ease + intensity; drift always on; optional impact nudges (<= 4 px) on anchors.
Match cut between a layer of this shot and one of the next.
Lower-third caption for a source, term, speaker or location.
Draw an SVG path (stroke reveal; RTL by default for Arabic layouts).
A panel of 1-6 KPIs with status colours.
A payload travelling through 2-8 stations; a station can fail and be fixed.
Deep-Dive entry card with parent chapter and prerequisite concepts.
